simple_definition: The part of a chip's final price that each step of the chain creates, after subtracting what that step bought from others; used to say how much of the industry each country 'owns'.
technical_definition: SIA/BCG: revenue-based activity shares (design, EDA/IP, equipment, materials) attributed to company HQ plus capacity-based shares (fab, ATP) attributed to facility location; CSET: segment value add weighted by firm-HQ market shares; OECD: national-accounts value added by producing economy (ICIO).

simple_definition: Two ways to give a factory to a country: by where the owning company is based, or by where the factory physically stands.
technical_definition: Location basis assigns fab/ATP capacity to the country of the site (SIA/BCG fab and ATP rows, SEMI, OECD); HQ basis assigns it to the owner's home (CSET, Knometa company shares). E.g. China hosted ~19% of IC capacity at end-2023 but Chinese companies held ~11%.

simple_definition: A way of counting factory output as if every wafer were the 200mm (8-inch) size, so factories using different wafer sizes can be added up.
technical_definition: Normalises wafer starts by wafer area to 200mm; a 300mm wafer counts as 2.25 equivalents. Used by SEMI World Fab Forecast, OECD and Knometa. Shares are unchanged by the choice of 200mm vs 300mm basis; absolute counts differ by 2.25x.

simple_definition: Factory capacity that has been announced or is being built but is not yet making chips.
technical_definition: OECD: 'planned' (announced, incl. construction starting 5+ years out) plus 'under construction' (being built or equipped), as distinct from 'in-production' (incl. first-silicon runs).
